models_evaluated: Skin cancer detection smartphone app CNN (unnamed commercial app)

links.outcome: Diagnostic performance across smartphone models and image capture in user hands
links.effect: Image-capture success in user hands was 28.9%; diagnostic performance varied between smartphone models.
links.quote: A substudy demonstrated low image-capture success in user hands (28.9%) and variation in diagnostic performance between smartphone models.

links.outcome: Image capture failure under real-world clinical conditions
links.effect: Image capture failed for 16.6% of lesions (317/1904) despite optimal conditions.
links.quote: Image capture was unsuccessful in 16.6% of lesions (n = 317/1904), despite optimal conditions.

links.outcome: Sensitivity and specificity of CNN alone vs CNN plus teledermatology review
links.effect: CNN alone: sensitivity 82.5%, specificity 76.8%. With teledermatology review: specificity rose to 86.8% (P < 0.001) but sensitivity fell to 75.3%.
links.quote: Combined CNN and teledermatology review resulted in increased specificity (86.8%; P < 0.001), with a sensitivity of 75.3%.

models_evaluated: Skin cancer detection app convolutional neural network (CNN; name not reported)

links.effect: Image-capture success in user hands was 28.9%.
links.quote: A substudy demonstrated low image-capture success in user hands (28.9%) and variation in diagnostic performance between smartphone models.

links.outcome: Diagnostic performance variation across smartphone models
links.effect: Diagnostic performance varied between smartphone models; device-specific estimates were not reported.
links.quote: A substudy demonstrated low image-capture success in user hands (28.9%) and variation in diagnostic performance between smartphone models.

links.outcome: Skin cancer detection sensitivity and specificity after teledermatology review
links.effect: Adding teledermatology review increased specificity from 76.8% to 86.8% (P < 0.001), while sensitivity decreased from 82.5% to 75.3%.
links.quote: Combined CNN and teledermatology review resulted in increased specificity (86.8%; P < 0.001), with a sensitivity of 75.3%.

links.effect: Diagnostic performance varied across different smartphone models used to capture the images.
links.quote: A substudy demonstrated low image-capture success in user hands (28.9%) and variation in diagnostic performance between smartphone models.

links.outcome: image-capture success in real-world user hands
links.effect: Image-capture success was very low (28.9%) when operated by users in real-world conditions.
links.quote: A substudy demonstrated low image-capture success in user hands (28.9%) and variation in diagnostic performance between smartphone models.

links.outcome: diagnostic accuracy of combined human-AI team
links.effect: Adding teledermatology review to the AI output increased specificity to 86.8% but resulted in a lower sensitivity of 75.3% compared to standalone metrics.
links.quote: Combined CNN and teledermatology review resulted in increased specificity (86.8%; P < 0.001), with a sensitivity of 75.3%.

screen.reason: Prospective clinical validation of a commercial AI skin cancer app evaluating diagnostic accuracy, variation across photographic conditions/users, and the effect of combining AI with clinician (teledermatology) review.
